data.value: Each of these is a collection of its own, with its own reading position. Where the editors state which part there corresponds to what you have read here, you can go on there from that part – by your own choice.

data.name: Account_Lead
data.value: An account is yours on every device: your list and how far you have read follow you. It asks for a name and a password – no mail address and nothing else about you.

data.name: Account_NeedsHttps
data.value: A password does not travel in the open: the account is reached over https only.

data.name: Account_Name_Hint
data.value: 3 to 40 characters: letters, digits, spaces, dots and hyphens. Others will see this name; it need not be your real one.

data.name: Account_Password_Hint
data.value: At least 12 characters. A sentence of your own is a good password.

data.name: Account_Register_Privacy
data.value: The site keeps the name and a value derived from the password – never the password itself. It knows no mail address of yours: if you lose the password, only your recovery codes let you in again.

data.name: Account_Recover_Lead
data.value: One of your recovery codes lets you choose a new password.

data.name: Account_Reopen_Lead
data.value: A closed account is kept for 30 days. Until then its name and password open it again.

data.name: Account_Codes_Lead
data.value: Write these down now and keep them in a safe place: they are shown this once. If you lose the password, each of them lets you in one time.

data.name: Account_CodesLeft

data.name: Account_Password_Note
data.value: With another password, every other device is signed out.

data.name: Account_NewCodes_Lead
data.value: Get new codes. The ones you have are worth nothing afterwards.

data.name: Account_Close_Lead
data.value: Closing signs you out everywhere at once. After 30 days the account and everything that belongs to it is deleted for good; until then its name and password open it again.

data.name: Account_Said_closed

data.value: An invitation is a link you pass on yourself – the site sends nothing to anybody. It makes an account for one person and nothing else: no connection between the two of you follows from it. It can be used for 14 days.

data.name: Account_Problem_invitations

data.name: Saved_Where_Account

data.name: Saved_Where_Offer
data.value: With an account your list follows you to every device.

data.name: People_Said_accepted

data.name: People_Said_declined

data.name: People_Said_ended

data.name: People_Said_circle-removed

data.name: People_Problem_later

data.name: People_Problem_kind
data.value: Please choose what you are to each other.

data.name: People_Problem_exists

data.name: People_Problem_declined-lately

data.name: People_Problem_too-many

data.name: People_Problem_circle-name
data.value: A circle needs a name of 1 to 40 characters that you have not used yet, and you can have 20 circles.

data.name: People_Circle_Empty

data.name: Person_None

data.name: Trees_None
data.value: You have no family tree yet, and none is shared with you.

data.name: Trees_Shared_Editor
data.value: {0} lets you see and change this tree.

data.name: Trees_Add_Note

data.name: Trees_Said_renamed

data.name: Trees_Said_person-removed

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-unknown
data.value: Both people have to be in this tree.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-same
data.value: A link is between two different people.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-exists
data.value: These two are linked like this already.

data.name: Trees_Problem_link-loop
data.value: That would make somebody their own ancestor.

data.name: Tree_People_None
data.value: Nobody is in this tree yet.

data.name: Tree_Links_Few

data.name: Tree_Members_Title
data.value: Who may see or change this tree

data.name: Tree_Members_Nobody
data.value: Once somebody has accepted a relationship with you, you can name them here.

data.name: Tree_Claim_Waits
data.value: You said this is you. It waits for the answer of who made the record.

data.name: Tree_Claim_NotMe
data.value: This is not me after all

data.name: Trees_Said_claimed
data.value: You said that this record is you. Who made the record will answer.

data.name: Trees_Said_claim-confirmed
data.value: Confirmed. The record names the account now.

data.name: Trees_Said_unclaimed
data.value: Taken back. The record names nobody.

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-taken
data.value: This record is another account already.

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-own

data.name: Trees_Problem_claim-nobody

Trees of others are named, not copied. No password is in it.

data.name: Photos_None

data.name: Photos_Problem_photo-large
data.value: The picture is larger than 10 MB.

data.name: Photos_Problem_photo-many

data.name: PublicTree_Lead
data.value: A family tree somebody made public. Everybody living it names has agreed to be named here.

data.name: Tree_Publication_Lead
data.value: A public tree is seen by everybody, with or without an account: its people, their years and how they belong together – not who it is shared with and not its history. It needs the agreement of everybody living it names. Somebody who has no account cannot agree, so a tree that names a living person without an account cannot be public.
